The files in this folder are data of ARPA Lombardia (ARPA - Regione
Lombardia), measured by its weather stations and published on the open-data
portal of Regione Lombardia, https://www.dati.lombardia.it, in the datasets
"Stazioni Idro Nivo Meteorologiche" (nf78-nj6b) and "Dati sensori meteo"
(647i-nhxk), under Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal (Public Domain
Dedication), https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/, as the
portal's records of both say (read 2026-11-22). They are not covered by the
licence of the code around them.

They were recorded on 2026-11-22 from https://www.dati.lombardia.it/resource/,
without a key or token, with curl, one GET each, at the addresses the
adapter writes for a run at 08:33:12 UTC over the Alps' box (5.0 to 17.2° E,
43.5 to 48.5° N). requests.txt lists them, a tag and an address a line, as
they were sent; a test holds the adapter's plan against it. The answers hold
no personal data and no key.

    sensors.json    GET nf78-nj6b.json?$select=...&$where=...    124,918
                    asked at 08:33:13 UTC                         bytes,
                                                                  whole and
                    unchanged: 683 sensors in service of the four kinds
                    (wind speed, wind direction, temperature, humidity) at
                    250 stations, 132 of which have an anemometer

    values_1.json   CUT from the answers to the three requests of values,
    values_2.json   asked at 08:33:14 UTC, which were 737,927, 801,512 and
    values_3.json   197,948 bytes: 7,775, 8,472 and 2,096 rows of 58, 59
                    and 15 stations, the ten minutes from 02:30 to 07:00 or
                    07:10 by the portal's clock (UTC+1)

The answers are a JSON array whose rows are written one a line, each line
after the first beginning with ",". The cut keeps the rows of eight stations,
every one of their rows, in the answer's order, each line byte for byte as
the portal wrote it, joined as in the answer, with the answer's last newline:

    values_1.json   14 (Valfurva S. Caterina, no hygrometer), 1347 (Barzio
                    Piani di Bobbio), 1382 (Veddasca Monte Cadrigna):
                    379 rows, 36,025 bytes
    values_2.json   629 (Crema, with 50 values marked "NA"), 1680
                    (Vilminore di Scalve Presolana), 1650 (Bormio
                    eliporto): 483 rows, 45,914 bytes
    values_3.json   857 (Santa Margherita di Staffora Passo del Giovà),
                    848 (Livigno La Vallaccia): 303 rows, 28,632 bytes

They were chosen for what they show: a station without a hygrometer, values
the agency marks invalid, stations in the first region's box, in the
southern and in the western one. The cut was made by a script that split
each answer between its lines and checked that every piece, read as JSON,
is the row of the whole answer it was cut from.

sensors_evening.json and values_evening.json are a sample for the server's
development mode, whose clock stands at 19:05 UTC on 2026-11-18, four days
before this source was recorded:

    sensors_evening.json   sensors.json cut, in the same way, to the 11
                           sensors of stations 14 (Valfurva S. Caterina),
                           1090 (Valdisotto Bormio 2000) and 1091 (Livigno
                           Mottolino): 2,041 bytes
    values_evening.json    CUT from the answer to the address the adapter
                           writes from sensors_evening.json for a run at
                           19:05 UTC on 2026-11-18 over the first region's
                           box, asked at 08:33:42 UTC on 2026-11-22: 640,988
                           bytes, 6,726 rows from 13:00 on the 18th to 06:50
                           on the 22nd by the portal's clock. The cut keeps
                           the rows up to 2026-11-18T18:30:00.000: 439 rows,
                           41,778 bytes

The address has no end in time, so the portal answered with every value
since. Which of them it had at 19:05 UTC on the 18th is its own record of
when it took each row in (`:updated_at`, asked for each ten minutes on
2026-11-22): the values of 18:30 by its clock (17:30 UTC) arrived at
17:42:04 UTC, those of 18:40 at 23:25:08 UTC. So every value in the sample
is one the portal gave, for the station and the ten minutes it says, and
the portal had the ten minutes of every one by 19:05. Whether a value was
changed after it arrived (the portal rewrote these rows the next night) is
not known. The hygrometers of 1090 and 1091 are in the list and gave no
value in those four days.

sensors_damaged.json and values_damaged.json are not the portal's data:
they are the evening sample with things changed by hand, to test how the
adapter reports what it cannot read. The test that uses them says what was
changed.

To record them again: run the adapter's plan for a moment and a box, fetch
the list of sensors and then the addresses of values the adapter writes from
it, write requests.txt, cut the values as above; set the moment in
tests/pipeline.rs; run the tests with VENTI_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 and review what
changed. The counts the tests pin will differ. The evening sample stays as
it is for as long as the development mode's clock does. The values dataset
holds the current month only: should the clock move, the sample can be made
again only within the month of the new moment.

A value in these files is what an instrument reported. It is no statement
that a place can be flown.
